$comment: The single definition of every version we track upstream. A Dockerfile ARG, a seam manifest, a peerDependency and a release manifest that each carried their own copy meant 'bump the pin' was four edits and one of them was always missed. Tests assert every derived copy equals the value here; the nightly compatibility matrix is one job that loops over these keys.

pandoc.notes: The document renderer's tested Linux version. Both runtime images and CI install the official architecture-specific Debian package through the same digest-checked renderer phase. Tool metadata is separate from the service contracts polled by the upstream matrix.

node.notes: LoopX 1.4.0 requires Node >=22.22.3 for its TypeScript control plane and for its SQLite goal store (node:sqlite; 22.22.3 embeds SQLite 3.51.3, which carries the WAL-reset fix the store relies on). The image's NODE_VERSION is exactly that minimum: a Node downgrade breaks LoopX.

dsh.notes: The 0.2 line's second release candidate (published 2026-09-29T09:56:27Z; npm's `latest` and `next` at adoption), adopted on 2026-10-14 on the criterion in decision #25 -- this version's running binary probed on the wire plus our own battery -- not on the tag. The audit that proposed it is .evimed-local/acceptance/course-correction-20261012/rectification-1014/A-plugins-and-upstream.md section 2.2 and the live run's evidence is in .evimed-local/acceptance/course-correction-20261012/live/r19-upstream/. `publishedBefore` is COMPUTED, never typed: `node scripts/ops/kernel-install.mjs cutoff --write` resolves the closure with npm (`--package-lock-only --ignore-scripts`), reads every member's publish instant from the registry and records the latest plus one minute. The rule it replaced, the CLI's own instant plus an hour, fenced `dsh-client-ui-settings-account` out of this very closure (re-published 80 minutes after the CLI). `cutoff --check` (pnpm check:kernel-cutoff, the kernel-seams workflow) fails when the recorded instant is not the computed one, and scripts/ops/test/fixtures/kernel-closure-times-<version>.json replays the computation without a network; moving the pin means recording the closure it resolves to. The nightly seam check installs through the same cutoff, and the nightly `candidates` job (scripts/ops/kernel-candidate-check.mjs, report only) diffs what the dist-tags name against this pin: composition, seams, unclassified wire methods, third-party peer ranges. What moved, and what we changed for it: (1) the closure went from 273 to 278 dsh* packages (+otel, +product-analytics, +host-product-telemetry-otel, +ui-settings-session-log, +experimental-schedule-bundle, none removed); cordis stays 4.0.4, the session format stays 4. (2) Three telemetry rows are new (`otel`, `desktop-product-telemetry`, `product-analytics`) and the session-telemetry collector's URL changed: each is `disabled: true` in our patch by value, not by upstream's profile-name expression, `productAnalytics/*` is a denied wire namespace, and a live kernel under a socket watch opened no connection outside the host. (3) `schedule`, `time-context` and `ui-schedule` left the web app's composition; `ui-settings-session-log` joined it and is hidden with its method ban. (4) The dump-config baseline was re-recorded (201 rows) after calibrating the seeding at the OLD pin until it reproduced the committed baseline byte for byte. (5) Five wire methods are new (`productAnalytics/enabled|report|watchPolicy`, `userQuestions/answer|attachWait`) and are classified; the hidden-panel pairing test now reads the namespaces each panel reaches from its own client bundle (packages/contracts/dsh/panel-remotes.json), which found `pluginInventory/*` open and denied it. (6) The golden frames were re-recorded from a live kernel with a real model; what changed against the 0.1.7 recording is listed in the evidence directory's golden-diff-report.txt. (7) The frame layer's kernel pins and its dictionary override moved (the running turn's header is `chat.deepDivingFor`; packages/contracts/dsh/client-locale.json is re-recorded). (8) The annotation bundle needs a build-time edit to stay Chinese under the product's locale id (`annotationCompatibility` below). Rolling back below this pin keeps every session written since (the format is unchanged) except `user-question-reply` messages that the experimental timed ask-user mode writes and 0.1.7 does not know; that mode stays off until the pin has settled. 0.2.1-alpha.2 is not adopted: cordis 4.0.5-alpha.1, `cotTranslation/*` unclassified, the LoopX plugin's peer range excludes it, and its `subagent` tool returns at once. `dsh plugin` manages a profile with pnpm and writes a pnpm-workspace.yaml listing the profile itself, which pnpm 9 refuses to add into without -w; this pin tracks DSH's own packageManager, not the workspace's. Upstream also tags prereleases on GitHub that npm never receives, so the matrix reports the GitHub tag as `upstreamTag` beside the npm `latest`: npm is what is installable and what `behind` means, the tag is the early warning.

annotationCompatibility.reason: The bundle picks its interface language by an exact match of the kernel's locale id (zh, en, ru; every other id is English, which its own test pins for fr, de and zh-Hans), and the product's locale id is zh-x-evimed: the annotation toolbar, its editor and the block it writes into the prompt turned English on the pin that brought 1.4.11. The edit makes it choose by the primary language subtag (zh-x-evimed -> zh); nothing else in the bundle changes.
annotationCompatibility.upgradePath: A build-time, digest-bound one-line edit of the pinned bundle's client.js (deploy/runtime-dsh/annotation-compat.mjs); a changed byte fails the image build by name, and the edit applied over its own output verifies the reverse transformation first. Drop it, and this record, when the bundle takes a regional or private-use tag of a language it ships as that language (the same defect for any Chinese-reading node, worth saying upstream), or when the product's locale is registered under an id the bundle takes as it is. Re-review on every annotation pin change; the sha256 is of the reviewed file.

openlist.notes: Self-hosted drive aggregator; v4.2.6 (2026-09-01), including access-control and authentication fixes from the current stable release. EviMed uses the pinned list, get and link contracts, then reads bytes through OpenList's same-origin proxy without following a provider-controlled redirect. The service runs with an isolated data volume and tenant-prefixed paths.

evimed-extract.recordedAgainst: the parser team's test environment (its address is not published; a deployment names its parser in OPEN_SCIENCE_DOCUMENT_PARSER_URL)
evimed-extract.notes: The team's own document-parsing API (docs/api/API.md v0.5.0, read at commit 83f79c4), which replaced the self-hosted MinerU container outright on 2026-09-20: no fallback parser, no comparison run, MinerU deleted in the same change. It is reached over HTTP with a Bearer key its own admin console issues (OPEN_SCIENCE_DOCUMENT_PARSER_TOKEN_FILE), text by Alibaba DocMind and bibliographic metadata by a model over the first and last 8,000 characters. `revision` is the label the knowledge-base index is keyed by, together with each file's SHA-256: the service reports no version of its own, so moving this label is what re-indexes every document parsed under the old one. `testServer` is the only address the owner gave and the compose default; production listens on 9021 per the service's env templates, on a host not yet named. The service is not polled by the nightly matrix (there is no release feed to poll); `contractAtPin` replays the fixtures recorded off the live server, and `scripts/ops/record-parser-contract.mjs` records the authenticated samples once the key exists.

openviking.notes: The context engine of the base stack, used three ways since v0.5.0 (2026-10-13; packages/contracts/openviking/README.md is the division of labour, capability by capability). (1) The derived recall index it has been since 2026-09-11: it ranks the research-memory records and the capsule facts whose authoritative rows stay in the control-plane PostgreSQL, under `memories/evimed/` — its `write` offers replace/append/create and no compare-and-swap, so the `expectedVersion` the record store enforces has no equivalent and those records are never its own. (2) Native memory: the engine extracts an account's memory from sessions with its own templates (deploy/web/openviking/memory-templates, eight types, the platform's keep / never-keep policy written in the engine's template language) and the official DSH plugin `plugin` reads it. (3) Knowledge: documents pushed as resources and compiled by the built-in VikingBot with the two official skills in `skills` into wiki pages and a graph. (2) and (3) are original data, so the volume is backed up (docs/WEB_OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md) and a rollback is a restore, never a downgrade: a v0.5.0 write is not readable by v0.4.x. MODEL PATH: the engine's `vlm` is this deployment's own model gateway, with a service bearer (`OPEN_SCIENCE_OPENVIKING_MODEL_KEY_FILE`), thinking off, non-streaming for extraction and summaries and streaming for the Compile agent; nothing in such a request names a user, so the spend is the platform's, booked to the internal project `evimed-openviking` under `memory-extraction` (root vlm) and `knowledge` (the Compile agent's own bearer, derived from the same key) and held by `OPEN_SCIENCE_OPENVIKING_MODEL_DAILY_BUDGET_CNY`. A 4xx from the gateway ends that commit for good (the engine does not retry it; a 429/5xx is retried 16 times in about 30 s). SHIM: in trusted auth mode v0.5.0 does not forward the caller's identity to its Compile runtime, so deploy/web/openviking/identity_shim.py (standard library, loopback 18791, stateless) adds the two identity headers; delete it, the entrypoint wrapper and `compile_api.base_url` on the first pin that forwards identity itself (upstream PR #5750, on main, in no tag yet). LIMITS AT THIS PIN: a compile target holds at most 128 typed pages and the check is destructive — the task still completes and the agent rewrites existing pages to pass it — so the scheduler stops submitting at about 100; `content/write` has no version precondition, so a write-back and a compile on one target must never overlap; a failed extraction commit is never retried by the server; task records expire after 24 h (7 d when failed); an OVPack carries no `k=v` tags. `skills.<name>.upstreamSha256` is the file at the tag (shipped as apps/server/src/openVikingSkills/<name>.skill.md, Apache-2.0); `installedSha256` is what the server stores after re-wrapping the frontmatter and dropping the final newline, and is what the startup check compares (`openVikingEngine.mjs`). `plugin` is the version in examples/dsh-memory-plugin/package.json at the tag; it has no runtime npm dependencies and its bundle row `openviking-memory-runtime` is inserted by its own cordis.patch.yml. `embedding` is what `scripts/ops/configure-production-state.mjs` renders into ov.conf (provider `dashscope` with `input: "text"`, which appends `/compatible-mode/v1` to `apiBase` itself and is the only provider that sends `dimensions`); changing the model or the dimension invalidates every stored vector, so it takes a `pnpm rebuild:memory-index --all` for the derived part and a reindex of the rest. `rerank` is read by the control plane, not by the server: `/search/find` never reranks, so the reranker runs where the hydrated text already is and the ov.conf carries no rerank section. A find score is (cosine + 1) / 2 since v0.4.22 and unchanged at v0.5.0 (production volume rehearsed 2026-10-12: same entries, same hits, scores = (old + 1) / 2), so `OPEN_SCIENCE_MEMORY_SEARCH_MIN_SCORE` stays 0.75. The server is AGPL-3.0 and runs unmodified as its own service; the CLI, plugins, skills and examples are Apache-2.0. The container tag carries a `v` prefix the PyPI version does not; the unprefixed tag does not exist and a compose file that names it fails at pull. Releases land every few days and have moved data layouts before, so the pin moves only through the matrix and the contract fixtures.

pgvector.notes: The control plane's PostgreSQL image since 2026-09-20: the official postgres:16 bookworm image with the pgvector extension added, so the data directory (/var/lib/postgresql/data) carries over from postgres:16.14-bookworm unchanged. Needed by the knowledge-base index's vector leg; without the extension that leg is skipped and kb_search answers mode "keyword", nothing fails. 0.8.x rather than earlier because 0.8 added iterative index scans, which keep a filtered nearest-neighbour search (one account's documents out of everyone's) from returning fewer rows than asked for. Read off Docker Hub on 2026-09-19: 0.8.6-pg16-bookworm is the newest 0.8.x tag, its image config says PG_VERSION=16.15-1.pgdg12+2 (not below production's 16.14), and the digests are the index and the linux/amd64 manifest. The extension is not marked trusted, which is fine here: the image entrypoint creates POSTGRES_USER as a superuser, so the application's migration creates it on first start and the backup restore drill can recreate it; pg_trgm (trusted, part of every postgres image) is created the same way. Moving this pin is a host step as well as a PR: back up, swap the image, and let the migration or the operator run CREATE EXTENSION.

knowledge-plugin.notes: The knowledge-source plugin (evimed-knowledge-plugin): the plugin team's own service that owns everything between the outside world and a normalised entry for the frontier feed (「前沿动态」) — the source registry, scheduling, fetching, parsing, per-source de-duplication, enrichment and source health — and that the control plane only ever pulls from (apps/server/src/knowledgePluginClient.mjs; the plugin never calls the platform). What is pinned here is the contract, not a build: `version` is the OpenAPI document's own version, whose canonical copy lives with the plan in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-21-medical-frontier-feed-assets/contract/ and is vendored byte for byte as `contractFile`, a test holding the two equal. The image is the plugin team's: until they have a registry it is built on the serving host from 项目代码/knowledge-plugin by scripts/ops/host-knowledge-plugin-build.sh, tagged with the plugin's own version and the release it was built from, and named in the deployment's .env as EVIMED_KNOWLEDGE_PLUGIN_IMAGE (deploy/web/docker-compose.knowledge.yml refuses to start without it), so no build is written here. The platform checks the contract major: the client compares the manifest's contract.version with OPEN_SCIENCE_KNOWLEDGE_PLUGIN_MIN_CONTRACT (default 1.0 — the same major, at least that minor), and the stream of a plugin speaking another major is not pulled until its manifest names a compatible contract again, while readiness warns frontier_plugin_incompatible and never turns red. Within major 1 the contract only grows (its rule 1), so a minor bump is additive and the platform ignores what it does not know yet. Moving this pin is re-vendoring the YAML and re-recording the fixtures off a live plugin with packages/contracts/knowledge-plugin/fixtures/record.mjs — never editing a fixture by hand. 1.3.0 (2026-10-05, flywheel F09) added one field to a source row, `platform_produced`: the source's content is the platform's own (the evidence feed the plugin reads like any other publisher's); the platform shows its items as 「EviMed 出品」 and never counts them as independent corroboration. A minor only adds, so the stream's recordings stayed as recorded and `record.mjs --platform-source` recorded again only what the minor changes (manifest, health and the one source row), off a live plugin of 1.3.0, which provenance.json says (`partialRecordings`). 1.4.0 (2026-10-10, review D-10) added one field to the health answer, `host_budget`: today's (UTC) requests against each host's own daily cap, `{host: {used, cap}}`. A spent cap makes the plugin refuse that host's polls until 00:00 UTC as its own decision, which counts against no source's health, so the table is the only place the spend shows; the platform exports it as open_science_frontier_plugin_host_budget_used / _cap and alerts on FrontierHostBudgetNearCap (used / cap > 0.9 for thirty minutes). It also states what `last_ok_fetch_at` counts: a 204, or a body with nothing in it, is the source's failure and not a read, where a page that parsed to no entries still is. Again a minor only adds, so the stream's recordings and the source row stayed as recorded and `record.mjs --host-budget` recorded again the manifest and the health answer, off a live plugin of 1.4.0, which provenance.json says (`partialRecordings`). There is no release feed to poll: the nightly matrix reports the upstream as unknown and replays the recorded fixtures at the pin (contractAtPin).

dashscope.notes: The independent reviewer (plan 2026-09-22, tiered review): Qwen3.8-Max on DashScope's OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, called by the control plane only (apps/server/src/reviewModel.mjs) with the operator's DashScope key file — the runtime holds no key. The snapshot is pinned, not the parent `qwen3.8-max`, because whatever the reviewer's findings are calibrated against is a version. Recorded on the live wire on 2026-09-23 (packages/contracts/dashscope/fixtures): `/models` lists `qwen3.8-max` and `qwen3.8-max-0902`; the dated alias `qwen3.8-max-2026-09-02` answers as `qwen3.8-max-0902`; an unknown snapshot is 404 `model_not_found`; thinking is on when `enable_thinking` is absent; `enable_thinking: false` and `thinking_budget` are honoured without streaming; strict `json_schema` is honoured with thinking on and off; reasoning tokens are counted in `completion_tokens` (`completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`); cached prompt tokens are `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`. With thinking off the model paraphrased an `evidence` field instead of copying it — the verbatim check lives in code (@evimed/domain reviewFindings). Price (the model's page, 2026-09-23): input ¥12, output ¥36, implicit-cache hit ¥1.5 per million tokens, no night rate — REFERENCE_PRICE_LIST evimed-reference-2026-09-23. thinkingBudget 16000 (raised from 8000 the same day): both live editor passes over a real 64 KB package spent all 8,000 reasoning tokens, and the two answered differently — 13 findings and no checklist, then 4 findings and all 19 checklist items; a 3-claim package spends 1.4–2.7k, so the ceiling only binds where it was binding.

typesafe.notes: TypeSafe's Jev (a System One model: typed questions over a text state, answered with probabilities; it generates no text) as the first pass of the reply check, L1 (apps/server/src/replyCheckJev.mjs, jevModel.mjs; the owner's decision of 2026-09-24). Called by the control plane only, with the operator's key file (OPEN_SCIENCE_TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE, mounted from OPEN_SCIENCE_TYPESAFE_API_KEY_HOST_FILE; unset binds /dev/null, which is no key and Jev off) — the runtime holds no key. The exact version is pinned, never `jev-latest`: TypeSafe's own models page says to pin the version a confidence threshold was tuned against, config.mjs refuses a pin that is not jev-X.Y.Z, and the client discards an answer from any other version. `supportConfidence` 0.8 is that threshold: a cited sentence Jev answers `supports` at or above it, naming no medicine, is recorded supported without a reviewer call; every other sentence goes to Qwen3.8-Max as before. Measured twice on the 101 claim/quote pairs of the 2026-09-21 probe (40 real matrix rows, 40 wrong-sentence, 11 changed-number, 10 negated): pairwise that day 98/101 exact; in the shipped form on 2026-09-24 — about fifty pairs to a request, each sentence with its own sources under its own key, every wrong-sentence pair in the same request as the passage that truly supports it — 100/101 exact, and at 0.8 Jev settled 37 of the 40 true supports with no false settlement. The one false `supports` sat at confidence 0.73 (0.64 pairwise); a gate of 0.7 would have settled it. Confidence is (k·p_max − 1)/(k − 1) of the answer's own probabilities (docs.typesafe.ai/confidence), and code re-derives it before it gates anything. `maxRequestTokens` and `maxStateTokens` are the provider's ceilings (docs.typesafe.ai/models, 2026-09-24: 64k per request, 32k for the state plus the longest question); a request estimated over either is not sent, and the reviewer judges every sentence. Price: $0.042 per million input tokens, output free, no night rate — REFERENCE_PRICE_LIST evimed-reference-2026-09-24, converted at the CFETS central parity it fixes. Wire (packages/contracts/typesafe/fixtures, recorded 2026-09-24; first seen 2026-09-21): an answer carries `model`, `answers` and `usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens`; no key is 403 and a wrong key 401, both `authentication_error` (the documentation lists 401 only); a malformed request and an unknown model are 400 `api_usage_error` (the documentation says 422); no rate-limit or request-id headers; 0.2–1.0 s. Jev's documented weak spots — counting, numeric closeness, dates, a state full of material the question does not need, and a state that addresses the checker — are why it may only confirm support: it never raises a ⚠, never judges a medicine sentence, and nothing it says authorizes anything. Moving the pin is re-recording the fixtures with packages/contracts/typesafe/fixtures/record.mjs and re-measuring the gate on the same corpus.

deepseek.notes: The research model: DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible chat API, reached only through the control plane's model gateway (apps/server/src/modelGateway.mjs) — the runtime holds no key. `model` is what a deployment runs when OPEN_SCIENCE_DEEPSEEK_MODEL is unset, and what the release receipt certifies end to end; `certified` is the gateway's allowlist (`supportedDeepSeekModels`): readiness refuses to serve and the runtime refuses to launch on any other name. Until 2026-09-27 the model was written only in the gateway, config.mjs, .env.example and compose, with nothing holding them equal (platform audit I1-13); packages/contracts/deepseek now does, together with the frontier and memory-extraction defaults and the specialist engines' LLM_MODEL. Moving the pin is one edit here plus the gateway's constants, and a new release receipt against the new model. From DSH 0.1.7 the kernel reaches the model through the gateway's Anthropic Messages route (/internal/model/v1/messages -> DeepSeek's /anthropic/v1/messages), the only protocol 0.1.7's DeepSeek adapter speaks; the control plane's own callers stay on chat/completions. Both routes reserve and settle through the same usage ledger. 2026-10-17: `deepseek-flash` is served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 from that day, under the same name, method and price. Verified the same day: GET /models answered deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro to the controller's probe with this key; DeepSeek's own 'Your First API Call' page, read through its Fetch API while recording the tool fixtures (apps/server/test/fixtures/deepseek-tools/recorded-2026-10-17.json), says deepseek-flash 'is now served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, and the calling method remains unchanged', and that deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted, served by it and billed at the Flash price. The gateway's certification compares nothing beyond the model id: `supportedDeepSeekModels` holds names, the release receipt names the configured model, and the provider's own `model` field is recorded on each ledger row (observed_model) and never compared -- so `model`, `certified` and the price rows do not move; a release receipt signed before 2026-10-17 certified the earlier model behind the same name, and the next one certifies this one. The same day DeepSeek opened two tool APIs, `tools`: Search answers in the web-search gateway beside SearXNG and Bailian, Fetch is web_read's second reader (apps/server/src/deepseekTools.mjs); both are called only by the control plane with this key, never by a runtime, held to `requestsPerSecond` per account for each tool, and billed per successful request -- a 200 with a result -- at `cnyPerThousandRequests` (the yuan table of DeepSeek's zh-cn Search guide, read 2026-10-17; the English page's USD 0.75 is the same price for dollar accounts; price list evimed-reference-2026-10-17).

js-yaml.notes: Required security backport for YAML4 CPU bounds. Workspace and both pinned kernel/profile copies must match this package without changing the DSH namespace. The runtime build hook is integrated, not pending: deploy/runtime-dsh/runtime-yaml-security.mjs runs in both runtime images (Dockerfile and Dockerfile.agentbay) -- `global` patches the globally installed kernel closure once it is installed, and `verify` re-checks that tree and the pre-initialized profile after the profile seed, including the seal -- and scripts/ops/kernel-install.mjs and deploy/runtime-dsh/profile-kernel-pins.mjs read this one pin (apps/server/test/runtimeYamlSecurity.test.mjs and dshProfileKernelPins.test.mjs hold it). Only the single `js-yaml` entry is accepted; moving it is one edit here, with the package's integrity.

openmed.notes: No SDK serving, local model runtime or weights. Native implementations use the existing cloud gateway and VCR stores. Dataset and terminology rights are reviewed separately.

loopx.notes: The complete native DSH plugin and CLI. Built into the immutable runtime with upstream workflow skills, GoalBar and same-session continuation. Hosted bootstrap checks installed bytes instead of upgrading during a turn; telemetry is disabled. Goal lifecycle belongs to LoopX; tenant ownership, model billing and clinical evidence remain EviMed responsibilities. Moved from 1.3.1 to 1.4.0 on 2026-10-17 (R19, r19-upstream2a) after real goals on the pinned kernel with a real model, the CLI and the skills root read-only and Node 22.22.3: /loopx starts a goal, the GoalBar shows it, Pause and Start change its state, a continuation turn runs (route loopx-continuation, automated, charged to the researcher), the inbox item arrives, a goal made by 1.3.1 opens, pauses and starts under 1.4.0, and a new goal's SQLite authority store (HOME/.loopx/authority/sqlite-v0) is read back by a fresh process; the evidence is in .evimed-local/acceptance/course-correction-20261012/live/r19-upstream2a/. What 1.4.0 asks of a runtime: Node >= 22.22.3 on PATH (see runtimeTools.node), the project's writable HOME and TMPDIR, and one long-lived effect-runtime process of about 25 MB, which does not exit when idle (1.3.1's did not either). The same on 1.3.1 and 1.4.0: a conversation opened on a cold kernel shows no GoalBar until the page is reloaded (its first read answers session_unavailable and is not retried), and a GoalBar Start can answer that LoopX is unreachable or did not sync when the CLI is slow. To watch: after Pause pressed in a turn that then ends before its receipts are closed, 1.4.0 ran one automatic recovery turn while the goal was paused (1 of 2 samples; 1.3.1 ran none in 3; the recovery module is byte-identical in both, the entry skill is not). 1.4.1 and 1.4.2 (2026-10-15) are not adopted; adopting one is the same steps: a scratch install with install-loopx.mjs, the goal runs of r19-upstream2a/scripts/loopx-run.mjs, workflow-skills.json and this block. Both compatibility adaptations below act on the plugin archive, which did not move, and were seen working on 1.4.0 (the driver continued the goal; the pause note reached a busy model).

compatibility.reason: Accept the recorded tool-role activation envelope of pinned DSH 0.1.7. After a verified GoalBar pause, explain the user action to the current model step without waking an idle session.
compatibility.upgradePath: Both adaptations are build-time, digest-bound edits of the pinned plugin archive (deploy/runtime-dsh/loopx-compat.mjs); a changed byte fails the image build by name. Drop the driver adaptation when the plugin pin recognizes the DSH 0.1.7 tool-role result, or when the DSH pin moves to a kernel that records the user/tool-result envelope; drop the pause adaptation when the GoalBar itself tells a busy model that its owner paused the goal. Re-record packages/contracts/loopx/goalbar-locale.json on any plugin pin change.
